1.1: Now behold the books of the secret of Elohim, the revelations of Ḥanoḵ. At that time, when three hundred and sixty-five years were fulfilled to me,
1.2: on a certain day of the second month I was alone in my house.
1.3: I was in great trouble, weeping with my eyes,
1.4: and was resting, asleep on my couch, and there appeared to me two very big men, such as I have never seen on earth;
1.5: their faces shone like the sun, their eyes were like burning candles, out of their mouths fire was coming forth, their clothes and singing were various, and their arms like golden wings, at the head of my couch, and they called upon me by my name.
1.6: And having awoken from my sleep I stood up
1.7: and bowed down to them and covered my face from terror.
1.8: And the two men spoke to me: “Have courage, Ḥanoḵ, do not fear; the eternal 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has sent us to you; behold, today you shall go up with us to the shamayim.
1.9: Tell your sons and your household all that they must do in your house, and let no one seek you till 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 returns you to them.”
1.10: And I listened and went out, summoned my sons Methushelaḥ and Regim, and told them all that those two men had spoken to me.

10.1: And the two men lifted me up from there, and carried me up to the north of the shamayim, and showed me there a very terrible place, all torture and torment;
10.2: at that place there was darkness and gloom, and there is no light there, but fire and flame, and obscurity comes down at that place,
10.3: and there is cold and ice and dungeons, and cruel, relentless messengers carrying arms and tormenting without mercy.
10.4: And I said: “How very terrible is this place!” And the two men answered me: “This place, Ḥanoḵ, is prepared for the dishonest, who work lawless things on earth, who practice witchcraft and sorcery and boast of their works,
10.5: who steal men’s souls secretly, who sever a binding yoke, who grow rich by doing violence, from the property of others, who, being able to feed, kill the hungering through famine, and being able to clothe the naked, took away their clothes,
10.6: who did not recognize their creator, but bowed down to vain elohim: for all these is this place prepared for an eternal inheritance.”

11.1: And the two men lifted me up from there, and carried me up to the fourth shamayim, and showed me all the courses and goings and all the rays of the light both of the sun and of the moon, their measurements and their goings, and I saw their goings.
11.2: The sun has sevenfold more light than the moon, and their circles are the chariots on which each of them rides just as the wind goes, and ever going and returning they have rest neither by day nor by night.
11.3: And I saw four great stars on the right of the sun’s chariot
11.4: and four on the left, going with the sun always, and messengers going before the sun’s chariot.

12.1: Flying spirits, each having twelve wings, and each of the messengers that rolls the chariot has twelve wings, carrying dew and heat, when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 commands them to descend to the earth with the sun’s rays.

13.1: And the two men carried me to the east of the shamayim and showed me the gates through which the sun goes up at the appointed seasons, and after the completion of every month, and after the shortening to the lengthening of the days and nights, six great gates,
13.2: and the greatness of the proportions of those gates, and I could not comprehend their greatness;
13.3: and of those through which the sun goes up and goes over to the west: through the first gates it goes out forty-two days, through the second gates thirty-five, through the fourth gates thirty-five days, through the fifth thirty-five, through the sixth gates …
13.4: at the going out of the season the years finish at the returns of the seasons.

14.1: And the two men carried me up to the west of the shamayim and showed me six great open gates after the eastern entrance and opposite it, through which the sun goes down there after the going up from the eastern gates,
14.2: and according to the number of days, thus it goes down through the western gates. When it goes out from the western gates, four messengers take the crown and carry it up to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
14.3: and the sun turns its chariot and goes out without light, and they put the crown on it again at the eastern gates.

15.1: The two messengers showed me this disposition of the gates by which it goes up and goes out. These gates 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 made for the taking of time and the counting of the years for the sun.

16.1: And they showed me the other, lunar, disposition, all its courses, and the two men pointed out to me all its circuits, and they pointed out to me its gates, twelve eternal gates to the east, through which the moon enters at the usual seasons,
16.2: thus also through the western gates after going round, and according to the number of the eastern gates.
16.3: Thus it goes down also through the western gates, and completes the year;
16.4: therefore it goes in the year with three hundred and sixty-four days complete, and therefore it is called outside the shamayim,
16.5: and the years are not reckoned in the number of the days, because the seasons of the year change.
16.6: And when they finish the western gates, it goes towards the eastern with its light. Thus their circle goes around like the shamayim, and their chariot, onto which the wind mounts in its course, and flying spirits draw along their chariot, six wings to each messenger. This is the lunar disposition.

17.1: And in the midst of the shamayim I saw armed troops serving 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 on cymbals and organs with incessant voice. And I was delighted listening to them.

18.1: And the men carried me up to the fifth shamayim, and I saw there many troops, Egoroi, and their appearance was like the human appearance, and their size greater than that of great giants.

19.1: And the two men took me from there; they carried me up to the sixth shamayim, and I saw there seven ranks of messengers, very bright and esteemed, their faces shining like the sun, and there is no difference in their faces, nor in their extent, nor in the composition of their clothes.
19.2: These organize and learn the good ordering of the world and the goings of the stars, of the sun and of the moon.
19.3: Messengers, messengers, these messengers of the shamayim harmonize all the life of the shamayim; they organize the commands, teachings and euphony, and singing and every esteemed praise.
19.4: And those messengers that rule over the seasons and the years, and the messengers that are over rivers and seas, and the messengers that are over the fruit and grass and everything bubbling,
19.5: and messengers who organize all the life of all people and write before the face of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
19.6: In their midst are seven phoenixes, seven keruḇim, and seven six-winged ones, voicing and singing to each other as one, and it is impossible to describe their singing, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 rejoices in His footstool.

2.1: And behold, my children, I do not know where I go, nor what will befall me;
2.2: and now, my children, do not turn away from Elohim; walk before the face of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and observe His judgments, and do not bow down to vain elohim, to elohim who made neither the shamayim nor the earth; they shall perish.
2.3: Keep your hearts true to the terror of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
2.4: and now, my children, let no one seek me till 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 returns me to you.

20.1: And the two men lifted me up from there and carried me up to the seventh shamayim. And I saw there a great light and all the fiery troops of incorporeal chief messengers and the shining station of the Ostanim, and I became afraid and began to tremble.
20.2: And the two men put me in the midst of them, saying to me: “Have courage, Ḥanoḵ, do not fear.”
20.3: They showed me from afar 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 sitting on His throne, and all the troops of the shamayim in companies stepping onto the steps, and they kept bowing down to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
20.4: and would then walk away and go to their places in joy and happiness and in immeasurable light;

21.1: and the esteemed ones serving Him do not leave Him by night nor go away by day, standing before the face of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and working His will, and all the troops of keruḇim and seraphim about His throne never leave Him, and the six-winged ones cover His throne, singing before the face of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
21.2: And when I had seen all, the two men went away from me, and from then on I did not see them. And they left me alone at the end of the shamayim, and I grew afraid and fell on my face.
21.3: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 sent one of His esteemed ones, Gaḇri’ĕl, to me, and he said to me: “Have courage, Ḥanoḵ, do not fear the troops; come after me, and stand before the face of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 into eternity.”
21.4: And I said to him: “Woe is me, my master! My soul has gone out of me for terror; call up to me the two men who brought me to the place, because I trusted them, and with them I go before the face of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”
21.5: And Gaḇri’ĕl seized me, just as a leaf is seized by the wind, and took me, and put me before the face of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.

22.1: and I fell prone, and could not see 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim,
22.2: and I bowed down to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim spoke to Miḵa’ĕl: “Take Ḥanoḵ, and take him out of his earthly garments, and anoint him with sweet oil, and clothe him in garments of esteem.”
22.3: And Miḵa’ĕl took me out of my garments and anointed me with sweet oil; and the appearance of that oil is better than great light, and its ointment like sweet dew, and its smell like myrrh, and it shines like the rays of the sun.
22.4: And I looked down at myself, and I was as one of the esteemed ones, and there was no difference. And the terror and trembling went away from me, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 with His mouth summoned me and said: “Have courage, Ḥanoḵ, do not fear; stand before My face into eternity.” And the archistratege of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, Miḵa’ĕl, brought me before the face of Elohim. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 tested His servants, and said to them: “Let Ḥanoḵ step up to stand before My face into eternity.” And the esteemed ones of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 bowed down and said: “Let him step up.”
22.5: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 summoned Vretil, one of His chief messengers, who is wise and writes down all the works of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
22.6: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Vretil: “Take the books from the safe places, and give Ḥanoḵ a reed, and tell him the books.” And Vretil hastened and brought me the books, all made sharp with myrrh, and gave me the reed out of his hand.

23.1: And he began to tell me all things in the shamayim and earth and sea, the courses and dwellings of all the elements, the seasons of the years, the courses and mutations of the days, and the commandments and teachings. And Vretil was telling me thirty days and thirty nights, his lips talking without ceasing. And I did not rest thirty days and thirty nights, writing all the signs, and when I finished, I had written three hundred and sixty books.

24.1: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 summoned me, and put me on His left near Gaḇri’ĕl. And I bowed down to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
24.2: And He spoke to me: All the things you have seen, Ḥanoḵ, standing and walking and completed by Me, I will tell you, before they took shape. First, all the things I created from non-existence into existence, and from invisible to visible.
24.3: And to My messengers I have not made known My secrets, nor told them the secrets nor their establishments, nor My endless and incomprehensible thinking out of creation.
24.4: And I opened up the light. And I rode through the midst of the light, just as one of the invisible, just as the sun rides from east to west;
24.5: and I conceived the thought to place foundations and to create visible creation.

25.1: I commanded in the very lowest that the very great Idoil should come forth, having in his belly a very great stone.
25.2: And I spoke to him: “Burst asunder, Idoil, and let the visible be born out of you.”
25.3: And he burst asunder. There came out of him a great stone, bearing all creation which I had wished to create, and I saw that it was good.
25.4: And I put a throne also for Myself, and sat down on it. I said to the light: “Go up higher and make yourself firm, and be a foundation for the highest.”
25.5: And there is nothing higher than the light, only nothing; and I saw, having bent Myself up from My throne.

26.1: I summoned a second time in the very lowest, and said that there should come out from the invisible into the firm one thing visible. And Aruchas came out, firm and heavy and very black. And I saw that it was well.
26.2: And I said to him: “Go below and make yourself firm.” And it became the foundation for the lowest. And under the darkness there is nothing.

27.1: Having surrounded some things with light,
27.2: I made thick and stretched forth a road of water over the darkness,

28.1: And I made great rocks firm, and commanded the bottomless waves to dry up on the dry land,
28.2: and on the rivers, having collected into one place the waters that fall into the bottomless sea, and binding them with a yoke, I gave an eternal boundary between sea and earth, that shall not be broken through by the water. And I made fast the firm, and founded the water over it.

29.1: And for all the troops of the shamayim I formed the sun out of the great light, and put it in the shamayim that it should shine over the earth.
29.2: From the stone I cut a great fire, and from the stone I created the incorporeal troops, and all the troops of stars, of keruḇim, seraphim and ophannim I cut from the fire.

3.1: And it happened, when I had spoken to my sons, that the two men summoned me, and took me on their wings and carried me up to the first shamayim and set me down there,

30.1: And the earth I commanded to bring forth all kinds of trees and high hills, all kinds of grass and all kinds of seed that are sown, before I created living souls, and prepared food for them.
30.2: And the sea I commanded to bring forth and give birth to its fishes, all kinds of reptiles that creep over the earth, and wild beasts and cattle, and all kinds of feathered birds.
30.3: And when I had finished all, I told My wisdom to create Me man.

31.1: And now, Ḥanoḵ, all the things I have told you, and all the things you have seen on earth, and all the things you have written in these books, I invented the creation of all this, having created from the highest to the lowest.
31.2: There is no counsellor here. I am eternal and not made with hands, and My thought is counsellor, and My word is deed, and My eyes behold all. If I look on all, then it stands, but if I turn away, then all will be destroyed.
31.3: Apply your mind, Ḥanoḵ, and know Him who speaks to you, and take the books that you have written.
31.4: And I give you the messenger Semil, and Rasuil, and him who brought you up to Me. And go down to earth and tell your sons all the things I have spoken to you and all the things you have seen from the lowest shamayim even up to My throne.
31.5: All the troops I have created; there is none that opposes Me or that does not submit to Me. All submit to My monarchy and serve My power.
31.6: And give them the books of your handwriting,
31.7: children to children, kinsmen to kinsmen, race to race, as mediator, Ḥanoḵ, of My general Miḵa’ĕl, because your handwriting and the handwriting of your fathers Aḏam and Shĕth shall not be destroyed till the end of time,
31.8: as I have commanded My messengers Orioch and Marioch, how that I have put a chart on earth, and ordered the ages that it be preserved,
31.9: and that the handwriting of your fathers be preserved, that it may not perish in the deluge which I shall make in your race.

32.1: For I know the wickedness of men, that they will not carry the yoke which I have laid upon them, nor sow the seeds which I have given them, but having cast off My yoke, they will take another yoke, and will sow empty seeds, and will bow down to vain elohim, and will reject My oneness,
32.2: and the whole earth will quake with injustice, wrongs, and fornication and idolatry.
32.3: Then also I shall bring a deluge onto the earth, and the earth will crumble together in great chaos.

33.1: And I shall leave over one just man with all his house, who shall work according to My will, and from their seed shall rise another race afterwards, very numerous and insatiable.
33.2: Then he who has brought up that race shall reveal the books of your handwriting and of your fathers,
33.3: through whom the guardians of the earth shall show them to the faithful men and shall tell them to that race, and it shall be esteemed thereafter more than before.

34.1: And now, Ḥanoḵ, I give you a term of waiting of thirty days to do all in your house; tell your sons all that your heart contains, that they may read and understand how there is no Elohim but Me,
34.2: and after thirty days I shall send My messengers for you, and they will take you from the earth and from your sons, whatever may be according to My will.

35.1: But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 summoned one of the messengers, the eldest of Tartarus, and put him by me, and the appearance of that messenger was as snow, and his hands were as of ice, and he chilled my face, because I could not endure the great heat and that terror. And thus 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to me.

36.1: For I am sent forth to you today from the mouth of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to speak to you all things that are and all that will be till judgment-day; and now, my children, not from my own mouth am I informing you today, but from the mouth of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
36.2: for you have heard my words from my mouth, but I have heard the words of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 like great thunder with incessant hurling of clouds; I have seen the raiment of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, infinite and incomparable, which has no end.
36.3: Now hear my words, telling of an earthly ruler, how fearful and miserable it is to stand before the face of an earthly ruler; it is terrible and miserable, because the ruler’s will is death, and the ruler’s will is life or great heat.

37.1: For, my children, I know all things from the mouth of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
37.2: This my eyes have seen from the beginning even to the end, and the dwelling-places of the clouds, both rain-bearing and thunderous.
37.3: And they showed me the messengers that guard them, and their keys.
37.4: I saw the treasure-houses of snow and of ice, and the going-up from where they go up in measure; they are carried up by a chain and let down by a chain, lest by heavy violence they tear asunder the clouds and destroy what is on earth, both air and frost. I beheld for a time how those who hold fast the keys fill the clouds full, and the treasure-houses are never exhausted.
37.5: I saw the lairs of the winds, how those who keep their keys carry weighing-scales and measures, and first put them in the weighing-scales and then in the measure, and let them out in measure over the whole earth, lest by their heavy breath they make the earth rock.
37.6: From there I was led to the judgment-place, and I saw hell all open, and the prisoners, and infinite judgment,

38.1: And having seen, I sighed and wept for the destruction of the impious, and I said in my heart:
38.2: “Ashrĕ is he who has not been born, or who, having been born, has not sinned before Elohim, that he may not have come to this place, nor have borne this yoke.”

39.1: And I saw the guardians of the keys of hell standing over against the gates like great serpents, their faces like lamps that have gone out, their eyes like darkened flames, and their teeth naked down to their breasts.
39.2: And I spoke to their faces: “I had better not have seen you, and may none of my tribe come to you.”
39.3: And I saw there a baruḵ place, and all baruḵ creatures, and all there living in joy and in infinite happiness in eternal life.
39.4: Then I spoke: “My children, and now I speak to you: Ashrĕ is he who fears Elohim and serves Him. And you, my children, learn to bring gifts to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, that you may enjoy life.
39.5: Ashrĕ is he who judges a judgment justly to the widow and orphan, and helps everyone that is wronged, clothing the naked with garments, and giving bread to the hungry.
39.6: Ashrĕ is he who turns back from the changeable path and walks along the straight path.
39.7: Ashrĕ is he who sows the seeds of righteousness, for he shall reap sevenfold.
39.8: Ashrĕ is he in whom is truth, that he may speak truth to his neighbor.
39.9: Ashrĕ is he in whose mouth is mercy and gentleness.
39.10: Ashrĕ is he who understands the works of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and esteems 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim.”

4.1: and brought me before the face of the elder, the ruler of the stellar orders, and he showed me all their courses and their passages from year to year, and he showed me two hundred messengers,
4.2: and he showed me there a very great sea, greater than the earthly sea, and messengers were flying with their wings.

40.1: Behold, my children, the things that can be used on earth and the things that have been planned I have written down from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim. Winter and summer, all have I put together, and of the years I have counted out the hours, and the hours have I all measured out and written down, and found out all the difference.
40.2: One year is more honorable than another, and one day than another, and one hour is more honorable than another. Likewise one man is more honorable than another, this one for much property, that one for mercy of heart, that again for understanding and cunning and for silence of tongue and mouth.
40.3: For there is none greater than he who fears Elohim; they shall be esteemed into eternity.

41.1: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 with His hands created man, and likened him to His own face. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim created all things great and small. He who brings the face of man into contempt brings the face of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 into contempt.
41.2: The anger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and great judgment are on him who spits in the face of man.
41.3: Ashrĕ is he who turns his heart towards such a man, so as to help the condemned and raise the broken.

42.1: He who multiplies lights before the face of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 will multiply their storehouses.
42.2: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim does not want bread nor candles, meal nor cattle, but by this means tests the heart of man.

43.1: For I swear to you, my children, that before man was, a judgment-place was prepared for him, and a measure and a weighing-scale in which man will be proved, and they are there already prepared.

44.1: And I shall put the work of every man in writing.
44.2: And now, my children, spend the number of your days in patience and gentleness, that you may inherit the endless age that is to come.
44.3: Every wound, every hurt and heat and wicked word that shall befall you, endure them for the sake of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim;
44.4: and if you are able to requite, do not requite your neighbor, because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is your requiter, and He will be the avenger on the day of the great judgment.
44.5: Lose gold or silver for a brother’s sake, that you may receive inexhaustible treasure on the judgment-day.

45.1: Stretch forth your hands to the orphan and to the widow, and according to your power help the poor,
45.2: and thus you shall find your reward on the judgment-day.
45.3: In the morning, at midday and in the evening and by day, it is good to go into the house of Elohim and to esteem the creator of all.

46.1: Ashrĕ is he who opens his heart and mouth for the praise of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
46.2: Cursed is he who opens his mouth for the humbling of his neighbor.
46.3: Ashrĕ is he who esteems all the works of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
46.4: Cursed is he who brings a creature of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 into contempt.
46.5: Ashrĕ is he who beholds the labor of his hands.
46.6: Cursed is he who looks to undo the labors of others.
46.7: Ashrĕ is he who keeps the foundations of his fathers.
46.8: Cursed is he who distorts the decrees and limits of his fathers.
46.9: Ashrĕ is he who goes and brings others together in peace.
46.10: Cursed is he who disturbs what is in peace.
46.11: Ashrĕ is he who speaks peace, and he has peace.
46.12: All this will be laid bare in the weighing-scales and in the books on the day of the great judgment.
46.13: And now, children, keep your hearts from all unrighteousness, that you may inherit the weighing-scale of the light into eternity.

47.1: Do not say, my children, that our father is with Elohim and will pray for us from our sins.
47.2: You see how I write down all the works of every man.
47.3: And none can distort my handwriting, because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 sees all.
47.4: And now, my children, mark well all the words of your father’s mouth,

48.1: that they may be for you an inheritance of peace; and the books which I have given you from Elohim, do not hide them; tell them to all who want them, that by word they may learn of the works of Elohim.

49.1: For behold, my children, the day of my term has approached; the messengers coming from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim urge the appointed time, and stand with me before my face.
49.2: And I shall go up tomorrow to the highest shamayim, into my eternal inheritance.
49.3: Therefore I command you, my children, that you do His good pleasure before the face of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.

5.1: He showed me the storehouse of cloud, from where it goes up and goes out, and showed me all the treasure-houses of snow and cold, and terrible messengers guarding the treasure-houses,

50.1: Methushelaḥ answered his father Ḥanoḵ: “What food is agreeable to your eyes, father, that we may make it before your face, that you may baraḵ our dwellings and your sons and all your household, and esteem your people, and thus after that depart?”
50.2: Ḥanoḵ said to his son: “Hear, my child: from the day when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 anointed me with the oil of His esteem, from that time there has been no food in me. I do not desire earthly food,

51.1: but summon your brothers and all our household, and the elders of the people, that I may speak with them and depart.”
51.2: And Methushelaḥ made haste and summoned his brothers Regim and Rim and Azuchan and Chermion, and the elders of the people, and brought all before the face of his father Ḥanoḵ. And he baraḵ them, and said to them:

52.1: “Listen, children: in the days of our father Aḏam, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim came down to earth
52.2: and visited it and all His creatures, which He created Himself, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim called all the beasts of the earth and all the wild animals and all the quadrupeds, and all the reptiles of the earth, and all the birds that soar, and brought them before the face of our father Aḏam, and called the names to all things that move over the earth.
52.3: And Elohim subjected to Aḏam all things existing into subservience, and secondly made them all dull, that they might be in subjection and obedience to man. For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 created man ruler over all His possessions.
52.4: In this there will be no judgment of every living soul, but only of man’s.
52.5: But for the souls of beasts there is in the great age one place and one fold.
52.6: For no soul of any animal which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 created will be shut up till the great judgment, and all souls will accuse the man,

53.1: whoever feeds the soul of a beast ill defiles his own soul.
53.2: But he who brings a sacrifice of clean beasts cures his own soul, and he who brings an offering of clean birds cures his own soul.

54.1: He who does injury to the soul of man injures his own soul, and there is no cure for him into eternity.
54.2: He who puts a man into paradise—his judgment shall not be exhausted into eternity.

55.1: Now, my children, keep yourselves from everything unrighteous which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 hates, still more from every living soul.
55.2: Just as man asks for his own soul from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, so let him do to every living soul, lest in the great age … He has prepared many mansions, very good dwellings, and bad dwellings without number.
55.3: Ashrĕ is he who departs into the sweet houses.

56.1: Ashrĕ is he who in his patience brings a gift before the face of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, for he shall find forgiveness of his sins.
56.2: When a man gives from his mouth terms of time to bring gifts before the face of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, doing thus he will find repentance of forgiveness. But if the appointed time passes by and he goes back on his word, he shall receive repentance.

57.1: When he covers the naked and gives bread to the hungry, he shall find forgiveness.
57.2: But if his heart murmurs, then he makes ruin of his giving of alms.
57.3: And if, when he has had his fill, he is contemptuous, then he shall lose all his good deeds,
57.4: and shall not find forgiveness, for every contemptuous man is hateful to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”

58.1: And it happened, when Ḥanoḵ had spoken to his sons and to the princes of the people, all the people and all those near him heard how 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim was calling Ḥanoḵ. All took counsel together, saying: “Come, let us kiss Ḥanoḵ.”
58.2: And these came together, up to four thousand men, and they came to the place Achuzan, where Ḥanoḵ was, and his sons.
58.3: And the elders of the people began to kiss Ḥanoḵ, saying: “Baruḵ are you of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the eternal ruler,
58.4: and now baraḵ your people, and
58.5: esteem us before the face of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has chosen you, and appointed you the taker away of our sins.” And Ḥanoḵ said to all the people:

59.1: “Hear, my children: before all creation took shape, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 appointed the age of things created. Then He created all His creatures, visible and invisible.
59.2: And then He put together man in His own image, and put into him eyes to see and ears to hear, the heart to reflect and the mind to deliberate.
59.3: Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 resolved the age for the sake of man, and divided up the various seasons and years and months and hours,
59.4: that man might reflect on the changes and end of the seasons, and the beginning and end of the years and the days and the hours, that he might reckon the death of his life.
59.5: And when the creation which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 created shall end,
59.6: and every man shall go to the great judgment of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, then the seasons shall perish, and from then on there will be no more years, nor months, nor days, and there will be no more hours from then on, nor will they be reckoned, but there shall begin one endless age.
59.7: And all the righteous shall be gathered together in the great age, and age and age of the righteous shall be gathered together, and they shall be eternal and incorruptible.
59.8: And from then on there shall be no labor among them, nor sickness nor humiliation, nor anxiety nor need, nor night nor darkness, but great, endless and indestructible light.
59.9: And the great paradise will be their shelter and eternal dwelling-place, and they shall no more bear the injuries of those on earth.

6.1: and he showed me the treasure-houses of the dew, like olive oil, and messengers guarding their treasure-houses, and their clothing like all the flowers of the earth.

60.1: And now, my children, keep your souls from all unrighteousness, such as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 hates.”

61.1: When Ḥanoḵ had talked to the people, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 sent down murk onto the earth, and there was darkness; it covered all the men standing with Ḥanoḵ.
61.2: And the messengers hastened and, having taken Ḥanoḵ, carried him up to the highest shamayim. And He received him, and put him before His face into eternity. And the darkness went off from the earth, and light came again,
61.3: and all the people saw, and did not understand how Ḥanoḵ had been taken, and esteemed Elohim. And they came to their homes, those who had seen such things. Esteem be to our Elohim into eternity. Amĕn.

7.1: And the two men placed me from there and carried me up to the second shamayim, and showed me there prisoners kept for the measureless judgment,
7.2: and I saw the condemned weeping, and I spoke to the two men who were with me: “Why are these tormented?” And the two men said to me:
7.3: “These are the apostates of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, not listening to the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, but taking counsel of their own will.”
7.4: And I was very sorry for them. And the messengers bowed down to me and said to me: “Man of Elohim, would that you might pray for us to Elohim!”
7.5: And I answered them: “Who am I, a mortal man, that I should pray for messengers? Who knows where I go, or what will befall me, or who will pray for me?”

8.1: And the two men placed me from there and carried me up to the third shamayim and set me down in the midst of paradise, a place unknown in goodness of appearance.
8.2: Every tree sweet-flowering, every fruit ripe, all manner of food perpetually bubbling with all pleasant smells, and four rivers flowing by with quiet course, and every growth is good, bearing fruit for food.
8.3: And the tree of life is at that place, at which Elohim rests when He goes up into paradise, and that tree is ineffable for the goodness of its sweet scent,
8.4: and another olive tree alongside was always discharging the oil of its fruit.
8.5: And there is no tree there without fruit, and every tree is baruḵ.
8.6: And the messengers guarding the paradise are very bright and serve 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 all days with incessant voice and sweet singing. And I said: “How very sweet is this place!”

9.1: And the two men answered me: “This place, Ḥanoḵ, is prepared for the righteous, who suffer offence in their lives and spite in their souls, and avert their eyes from injustice and make righteous judgment, to give bread to the hungering, to clothe the naked and cover them with a garment, to raise the fallen, and help the wronged, who walk before the face of Elohim and serve Him alone; for these is this place prepared for an eternal inheritance.”
